title: The base-change property $BC(f,n,q_0)$
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $n\ge1$ and $q_0\ge0$ be integers and put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$. Use the module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and the unbounded module derived categories and cohomology sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

Say that the *cumulative universal base-change property* $BC(f,n,q_0)$ holds if the following condition holds. For every morphism $a:S'\to S$, form $X'=X\times_SS'$ with its projection $f':X'\to S'$. For every quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism $g:T\to S'$, form the base-change square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xleftarrow{h}&Y=X'\times_{S'}T\\
f'\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow e\\
S'&\xleftarrow{g}&T,
\end{array}
\qquad f'\circ h=g\circ e.
$$
Here $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$ are the two projections. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$ annihilated by $n$, regard $F$ as a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules via $[m]s=ms$, and use the complex with $F$ in degree zero, zero in all other degrees and zero differentials, denoting its image in the derived category by $F[0]$. For every integer $q\le q_0$, require that
$$
\mathcal H^q\!\left(\operatorname{BC}_{f',g}(F[0])\right):
\mathcal H^q\!\left((f')^{-1}Rg_*F[0]\right)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal H^q\!\left(Rh_*e^{-1}F[0]\right)
$$
be an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X'_{\Et}$. The map $\operatorname{BC}_{f',g}$ is exactly the unbounded module base-change map of [sbc-def-base-change-map], namely the exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] read with $(f,f',g,g')=(g,h,f',e)$. Thus the direction is inverse image along $f'$ and direct image along $g$, with target direct image along $h$ of the inverse image along $e$.

This is the cumulative condition over all base changes of $f$, as opposed to the single-degree, fixed-base predicate of [sbc-def-base-change-property]. On the domain where $n$ is invertible on $S$, its nonnegative-degree conditions are the conditions $BC(f',n,q)$ of that node for every $0\le q\le q_0$ and every base change $f'$; here the quantifier $q\le q_0$ also explicitly includes negative degrees. The exchange used here is the same unbounded map already specified in [sbc-def-base-change-map], not a different map whose agreement is an extra part of this definition. No invertibility of $n$ on $S$ is required in the present definition.

lean.statement: def UnboundedCumulativeUniversalBaseChangeProperty {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) (q₀ : ℕ) : Prop
lean.note: Uses the recorded exact unbounded exchange interface of def-kun-unbounded-exchange on the exchanged canonical pullback square, with coefficients ULift (ZMod n), followed by DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor in every integer degree at most q₀. There is no invertibility restriction. The existing smooth-base-change cumulative predicate has an invertibility parameter and only quantifies over nonnegative degrees, so is not an exact attachment.
